user-story.i-want: Annie to proactively suggest helpful triggers during conversation
user-story.so-that: I can benefit from proactive features without needing to know they exist

ac.title: Proactive Capabilities Section
ac.then: includes: - Explanation of proactive capabilities - When to offer triggers (signal phrases) - Schedule translation examples (natural language → cron) - Best practices for trigger creation - How to manage existing triggers

ac.title: Active Triggers in Context
ac.then: - Includes summary of active triggers - Shows intent_name, schedule/condition, last fired - Helps LLM reference existing triggers

ac.title: action_context Guidance
ac.then: - Prompt teaches comprehensive action_context structure - Emphasizes this is briefing for future LLM - Lists required sections

key-content.signal-phrases: - "remind me..." / "let me know when..." / "alert me if..." - "check in with me..." / "wake me up..." - "every morning/evening/week..."
key-content.schedule-translations: "every morning" → 9 AM daily "every weekday morning" → 9 AM Mon-Fri (cron: "0 9 * * 1-5") "every Friday" → Friday 9 AM or 5 PM "market open" → 9:30 AM ET weekdays "in 2 hours" → One-time calculated
key-content.action-context-sections: - original_request (user's exact words) - intent_summary (1-3 sentences) - user_context (invariant preferences only, NO dynamic data) - execution_instructions (step-by-step guide for wake-up LLM) - message_guidance (tone, length, examples, edge cases) - available_tools (what to call and when) - edge_cases (unusual situations) - meta (created_at, notes)

stream-route-usage.code:
from api.prompts import build_system_prompt
system_message = build_system_prompt( user_id=user_id, platform=platform, include_tool_instructions=True, profile=profile, portfolio=portfolio ) if user_id else None
stream-route-usage.context-gathering: Profile: Retrieved via ProfileManager.get_cached_profile() (lines 993-1018) Portfolio: Retrieved via PortfolioManager.get_cached_portfolio() (lines 993-1018) Pattern: Both use Redis-cached data with smart refresh

profile-manager.usage: profile_manager = ProfileManager(redis_client) profile = await profile_manager.get_cached_profile(user_id) # Returns: Dict[str, Any] or None # Cached for 15 minutes (PROFILE_CACHE_TTL = 900s) # Background refresh every 5 messages or 15 min

portfolio-manager.usage: portfolio_manager = PortfolioManager(redis_client) portfolio = await portfolio_manager.get_cached_portfolio(user_id) # Returns: Dict[str, Any] or None # Cached for 5 minutes (PORTFOLIO_CACHE_TTL = 300s) # Shorter TTL due to more dynamic nature

task.title: Add proactive capabilities section to system prompt
task.action: Create new constant PROACTIVE_CAPABILITIES_SECTION with content from design doc Section 6.1 (lines 1107-1174). Include: - When to offer proactive features (signal phrase table) - Best practices for creating triggers (clarify, confirm, explain, offer) - Schedule translation table - Managing existing triggers guidance - Writing good action_context guidance
task.integration: Add to build_system_prompt() after BASE_SYSTEM_PROMPT but before user-specific data. This makes it part of the core personality/capability description.

task.title: Add action_context guidance section
task.action: Create new constant ACTION_CONTEXT_GUIDANCE with comprehensive structure documentation: - All required sections (original_request, intent_summary, user_context, etc.) - Critical warnings about NOT snapshotting dynamic data in user_context - Examples of good vs bad patterns - Emphasis that action_context is for future wake-up LLM
task.integration: Include this in PROACTIVE_CAPABILITIES_SECTION as the "Writing Good action_context" subsection. Reference design doc Section 4 (lines 378-836) for complete structure.

task.title: Implement active triggers injection
task.action:
1. Create format_triggers_for_prompt(triggers: List[Dict]) -> Optional[str]: - Input: List of trigger dictionaries from IntentsClient - Output: Formatted string like design doc Section 6.2 (lines 1180-1189) - Format: "1. {intent_name} - {schedule/condition} - Last fired: {time}"
2. Update build_system_prompt() signature: - Add parameter: triggers: Optional[List[Dict[str, Any]]] = None
3. Add injection logic in build_system_prompt(): if triggers: triggers_str = format_triggers_for_prompt(triggers) if triggers_str: prompt_parts.append("\n\nYOUR ACTIVE TRIGGERS:") prompt_parts.append(triggers_str)
task.dependencies: BLOCKS: Story 13.1 (IntentsClient) must be complete to fetch trigger data. This story can implement the formatting function, but injection requires 13.1.

prompt-placement-strategy.order: 1. BASE_SYSTEM_PROMPT (core personality) 2. PROACTIVE_CAPABILITIES_SECTION (new - core capability) 3. user_id 4. USER PROFILE (dynamic user data) 5. USER PORTFOLIO (dynamic financial data) 6. YOUR ACTIVE TRIGGERS (dynamic trigger list) 7. Current date/time 8. Platform-specific formatting 9. TOOL_USAGE_INSTRUCTIONS
prompt-placement-strategy.rationale: Proactive capabilities go early (after personality but before user data) because they're a core system capability, not user-specific. Active triggers come after profile/portfolio because they're dynamic user state like portfolio.

formatting-pattern.header-style: Use "## SECTION TITLE" for top-level sections (matches current pattern) Use "### Subsection" for nested sections
formatting-pattern.table-rendering:
Signal phrases table should be plain text, not markdown tables (better for LLM consumption):
"Listen for these signals: - 'I want to keep an eye on...' → Offer condition trigger - 'Remind me every morning...' → Offer scheduled trigger ..."

trigger-summary-format.example: 1. "Morning portfolio brief" - Weekdays 8:30 AM PT - Last fired: yesterday 2. "NVDA price alert" - When NVDA < $130 - Never fired yet 3. "Weekly check-in" - Fridays 5 PM PT - Last fired: 2 days ago

intents-client-interface.expected-api:
# From Story 13.1 - IntentsClient from api.intents_client import IntentsClient
client = IntentsClient()
# Get active triggers for user triggers = await client.get_active_intents(user_id) # Returns: List[Dict[str, Any]] or []
# Each trigger dict contains: { "intent_id": "uuid", "user_id": "telegram_12345", "intent_name": "Morning portfolio brief", "trigger_type": "scheduled", # or "condition" "schedule": { # if trigger_type == "scheduled" "mode": "cron", "expression": "0 8 * * 1-5", "timezone": "America/Los_Angeles" }, "condition": { # if trigger_type == "condition" "type": "price", "expression": "NVDA < 130" }, "action_context": {...}, "enabled": true, "last_fired_at": "2025-12-23T08:30:00Z", "created_at": "2025-12-01T10:00:00Z" }
intents-client-interface.error-handling: Graceful degradation: If IntentsClient fails, triggers should be None and prompt should build without YOUR ACTIVE TRIGGERS section. Same pattern as profile/portfolio fetching.

token-budget-consideration.concern: Adding proactive section + trigger list increases prompt tokens. Need to balance detail with efficiency.
token-budget-consideration.mitigation: - Proactive section: ~500 tokens (one-time, always present) - Trigger list: ~50 tokens per trigger (dynamic, user-specific) - Expected: Most users have 0-5 triggers, so 0-250 tokens - Total addition: ~500-750 tokens - This is acceptable given improved proactive suggestions
token-budget-consideration.monitoring: Verify in AC: "Prompt additions don't significantly impact response latency" Can measure via Langfuse token tracking.

verification-steps.step: Test prompt contains proactive capabilities section: - Build system prompt with no user data - Assert "PROACTIVE CAPABILITIES" in prompt - Assert signal phrases present - Assert schedule translation examples present
Test action_context guidance present: - Assert "action_context" structure documented - Assert warning about NOT snapshotting dynamic data - Assert all required sections listed

Test trigger injection when user has triggers: - Mock IntentsClient.get_active_intents() to return sample triggers - Build system prompt with triggers parameter - Assert "YOUR ACTIVE TRIGGERS:" in prompt - Assert trigger summary formatted correctly
Test graceful degradation when no triggers: - Build system prompt with triggers=None - Assert "YOUR ACTIVE TRIGGERS:" NOT in prompt - Assert rest of prompt still works

Test LLM behavior (manual): - Send message: "Remind me every morning at 8am to check my portfolio" - Verify Annie offers to create trigger - Verify Annie explains what will happen - Verify Annie asks for confirmation
Test LLM knows existing triggers (manual): - Create a trigger for user - Send message: "What reminders do I have set up?" - Verify Annie can reference the active trigger from context
Test token impact (observability): - Compare average prompt tokens before/after this story - Use Langfuse to measure impact - Ensure latency doesn't increase significantly

enables.note: Enhanced system prompt teaches LLM how to use trigger management tools effectively. Wake-up agent benefits from comprehensive action_context guidance.

implementation-notes.incremental-approach: 1. Start with Tasks 1-2 (add prompt sections) - can complete immediately 2. Implement Task 3 (formatting function) - can test with mock data 3. Wait for Story 13.1 completion 4. Implement Task 4 (stream route integration) 5. Run full verification suite
implementation-notes.suggested-commit-strategy:
Commit 1: "Add proactive capabilities and action_context guidance to system prompt" - Tasks 1-2 complete - Update prompts.py with new sections
Commit 2: "Implement trigger summary formatting for prompt injection" - Task 3 complete - Add format_triggers_for_prompt() function - Update build_system_prompt() signature
Commit 3: "Integrate active triggers into stream route system prompt" - Task 4 complete (requires 13.1) - Update stream.py to fetch and pass triggers

edge-cases.case: User has many triggers (>10): - Consider limiting to most recent 10 in prompt - Or summarize: "You have 15 active triggers. Recent: ..."
IntentsClient fails during stream route: - Log warning, continue without triggers in prompt - Don't break the chat flow
Trigger has malformed data: - format_triggers_for_prompt() should handle missing fields gracefully - Use .get() with defaults, don't crash on KeyError
